To determine whether $f(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=c,$ we need to check whether the left-sided limit is equal to the function value.

The function has three discontinuities: $x=-2,$ $x=1,$ and $x=3.$

- At $x=-2$ the function is not left-continuous because it's undefined at this point. $\,\times $

- At $x=1$ the function is left-continuous because

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)=2=f(1).\,✓
$$

- At $x=3$ the function is left-continuous because

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{3}^{-}}f(x)=0=f(3).\,✓
$$

Therefore, from **left to right**, the function $f(x)$ is not continuous but is right-continuous at $x=1$ and $x=3.$
